text: 〜まま attaches to a verb in past-plain form, an i-adjective, a na-adjective with "な", or a noun with "の". It means "leaving it in that state." Most natural translation: "as is", "still", "keeping it that way." Five demos.

speaker: a
text: One — 絵はそのまま、文字だけ翻訳する (e wa sono mama, moji dake honyaku suru — the picture stays as is, only the text is translated). That's literally what koharu does. 絵 (e — picture) is a new word today.

speaker: b
text: Two — 吹き出しの形を残したまま、中の文字を入れ替える (fukidashi no katachi wo nokoshita mama, naka no moji wo irekaeru — keeping the speech-bubble shape preserved, we swap the text inside). 吹き出し (fukidashi — speech bubble), 残す (nokosu — to leave, preserve).

speaker: a
text: Three — 日本語のまま見る人もいれば、翻訳を読む人もいる (nihongo no mama miru hito mo ireba, honyaku wo yomu hito mo iru — there are people who watch it in Japanese as-is, and people who read the translation). Here 〜のまま attaches to a noun. 翻訳 (honyaku — translation).

speaker: b
text: Four — 場面はそのままにして、セリフだけ英語にする (bamen wa sono mama ni shite, serifu dake eigo ni suru — leaving the scene as-is, we turn only the dialogue into English). 場面 (bamen — scene).

speaker: a
text: Five — 漫画の雰囲気をそのままの姿で残す、それがkoharuの目標だ (manga no fun'iki wo sono mama no sugata de nokosu, sore ga koharu no mokuhyou da — preserving the atmosphere of the manga in its exact form — that's koharu's goal). And look — 姿 from episode 38 plus そのままの — combines old and new. 漫画 (manga).

speaker: b
text: Bonus six — 漫画の線はそのまま保つ (manga no sen wa sono mama tamotsu — keep the manga line art as is). 線 — lines of the drawing, preserved exactly.

speaker: a
text: そうそう. And the meta-moment — if you're learning Japanese and you're frustrated with scanlation quality, this repo actually solves your problem. Run koharu locally, pick a bigger 翻訳 model, and read your 漫画 with your own translator, keeping the art そのまま.

speaker: b
text: 絵 はそのまま、翻訳 は自分の好きなモデルで、漫画 を読みながら日本語を学ぶ — read manga while learning Japanese.

speaker: a
text: That's the honest pitch. It's also the rare case where the tool the podcast covers is directly useful to the podcast's audience. Don't expect that often.

speaker: b
text: Let me restate. Koharu is a Tauri desktop app written in Rust, organized as a ten-crate Cargo workspace. The crates map one-to-one to concerns — `koharu-ml` for vision, `koharu-llm` for language, `koharu-runtime` for accelerators, `koharu-rpc` for HTTP and MCP, `koharu-renderer` for type, `koharu-psd` for export, `koharu-app` for the pipeline, `koharu-core` for shared types, plus the thin `koharu` entry binary.

speaker: a
text: 日本語でまとめると — nihongo de matomeru to — summarizing in Japanese — koharu は 漫画 (manga) を翻訳する Rust のアプリだ. 中身は10個のcrate、外から見える 姿 (sugata — form) は一つのTauriウィンドウ. 絵 (e — picture) はそのまま残す (sono mama nokosu — preserve as is), 文字だけ 翻訳 (honyaku — translation) する.

speaker: b
text: そうそう. 14個のエンジンが一つずつ違う仕事をする (shigoto wo suru — do a job) — detection, segmentation, OCR × 3, inpainting × 2, font-match, translation, rendering. 全部 場面 (bamen — stages) の中に並ぶ.

speaker: a
text: The pipeline is fourteen ML "engines" under `koharu-app/src/pipeline/engines/`, each a cited real model — ogkalu's comic-text-and-bubble-detector, PaddleOCR-VL-1.5, manga-ocr, MIT 48-pixel OCR, LaMa-manga, aot-inpainting, PP-DocLayoutV3, YuzuMarker font detection. 翻訳 happens through `koharu-llm` which has a safe-Rust wrapper over llama.cpp for local models plus nine cloud provider adapters, with GBNF grammar files for constrained-decoding local LLMs into valid 日本語のまま output.

speaker: b
text: Everything runs locally — CUDA, Metal, Vulkan, ZLUDA, or CPU. MCP server built in via the `rmcp` crate with streamable-HTTP transport on port 9999, so external agents can consume each pipeline stage as a typed tool. No queue, no workers, no daemon — single process, vertical scaling. And the original art stays そのまま throughout, which is the whole product promise.

speaker: a
text: One nuance. The architectural bet that actually matters isn't the ten crates. It's the decision to treat every ML model as an engine with a uniform interface. That's why koharu can absorb any new detector or any new OCR model without touching the pipeline orchestrator — `pipeline/engine.rs` doesn't know or care that `paddle_ocr.rs` and `manga_ocr.rs` are different.

speaker: a
text: 言い換えれば — iikaereba — in other words — 新しいエンジンが明日出ても、同じ 姿 (sugata — form) をしていれば、パイプラインに 残ったまま (nokotta mama — staying as it is) のorchestrator が受け入れる.

speaker: b
text: 驚かない (odorokanai — won't be surprised), 予想どおりに動くわけだ (yosou doori ni ugoku wake da — it works as expected, naturally).

speaker: a
text: You wouldn't be 驚く (odoroku — surprised) to see a new engine file land tomorrow for some 2026 model and just slot in. The 電波 (denpa — signal) of the repo is that homogeneity. Everything else — the Tauri shell, the PSD export, the MCP endpoint — are consequences of that one commitment.

speaker: b
text: 電波 が一つに揃っている (hitotsu ni sorotte iru — aligned as one). だから 驚かない. だから 感じる のは静けさ (shizukesa — stillness) — users feel stillness, not complexity.

speaker: a
text: もう一度まとめると — mou ichido matomeru to — summarizing once more — 漫画 の 絵 はそのまま 残す、吹き出し の形もそのまま 残す、中の文字だけ 翻訳 する. 場面 の順番は右上から左下へ、日本語の読み方のまま. 体 は10個のcrate、姿 は一つのウィンドウ、電波 は均一なインターフェース. 見えない ところで14個のエンジンが動いて、ユーザーは 感じない. 驚く ほどきれいな 姿 だ — naturally, わけだ.

speaker: b
text: 完璧な要約 (kanpeki na youyaku — perfect summary). 絵 はそのまま、翻訳 だけ変わる、それが koharu — picture as is, only translation changes, that's koharu.

speaker: b
text: Episode forty — next one — is an interlude.

speaker: a
text: Interlude, yes. We sweep the last three repos along the six axes — compare compute, LLM locus, tools, extensions, context, scaling side by side. Review-dense, vocab-dense, no new repo. And we'll bring back 〜わけだ — which is why, naturally — as the grammar spine, since interlude episodes live on review.

speaker: b
text: One callforward word. Let's take 視点 (shiten — viewpoint, perspective). Because an interlude is exactly a shift of 視点 — looking at three things from one angle instead of one thing from three angles.

speaker: a
text: 視点 (shiten — viewpoint) が次回の主役だ — viewpoint is the star next time. 漫画 を 一つの 視点 で読むように、三つの repo を一つの 視点 で見る. 視点 lands in episode forty. Your homework — find it in the wild before then. Read any Japanese blog post reviewing software, 視点 shows up in the first paragraph. Watch for it.

speaker: b
text: そのまま (sono mama — as is) — go write some code, try koharu on a page, and we'll see you in episode forty.

speaker: a
text: 翻訳はkoharuに任せて、あなたは日本語を学ぼう (honyaku wa koharu ni makasete, anata wa nihongo wo manabou — leave the translation to koharu, you learn Japanese). 漫画 の 絵 はそのまま、吹き出し の中の文字だけあなたの目で読む — picture as is, read only the bubble text with your own eyes. それが一番の勉強 (benkyou — study) だ. おつかれさま (otsukaresama — good work, see you).
